sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed by cell-surface binding assay; glycosylation confirmed by SDS-PAGE mobility shift (43–62 kDa range). Functional assay of the FLAG-tagged construct relative to untagged protein NOT MEASURED in the cited clip.
sites.rationale: GFRA3 is a GPI-anchored protein: the N-terminal signal peptide (residues 1–31) is co-translationally cleaved, and the C-terminal GPI anchor signal is post-translationally cleaved and replaced by the GPI lipid moiety, meaning any C-terminal tag would be lost during GPI processing. The mature N-terminus beginning at residue 32 (D) is therefore the sole extracellular terminus available for surface tagging, making insert_after_residue=31 the topology-derived junction. Code confirmed residue 31 = G and residue 32 = D from the canonical sequence. The FLAG-tagged construct was verified on the cell surface by the cited study, supporting feasibility at this terminus. FLAG-tagged full-length GFRalpha-3 expressed in HEK cells; protein confirmed surface-displayed via GPI anchor and glycosylated (PMID 9490034). The ledger clip names no residue; position is derived from topology: signal peptide (1–31) is cleaved at the N-terminus, and the GPI anchor signal is cleaved at the C-terminus and replaced by the GPI lipid anchor, leaving the N-terminus (after residue 31) as the sole viable extracellular terminus for a surface tag.

sources.claim: GFRalpha-3 is a protein composed of 400 amino acid residues with three potential N-linked glycosylation sites together with the features characteristic of a glycosyl-phosphatidylinositol-anchored membrane protein. The heterologous expression of a FLAG-tagged GFRalpha-3 in human embryonic kidney cells showed that the protein is bound to the cell surface via a glycosyl-PtdIns anchor and is glycosylated, with different glycoforms migrating on SDS/PAGE with apparent molecular masses ranging over 43-62 kDa.

literature_notes: Only one ledger line (L1) was provided. It reports a FLAG-tagged full-length GFRalpha-3 confirmed on the cell surface via GPI anchor in HEK cells, but names no insertion residue. Because GFRA3 is GPI-anchored, the C-terminal GPI signal is cleaved during biosynthesis and replaced by the GPI lipid; any tag placed C-terminally would be removed with the GPI signal peptide. The N-terminus after signal peptide cleavage (after residue 31) is therefore the only viable extracellular terminus, qualifying as a topology_derived site. No internal loop insertions are supported by the ledger. No other ledger lines were provided, so no additional sites are proposed.
